one_line: A senior Eastern Ganga-era administrator overseeing coin minting, records and temple accounts in 11th–14th century coastal Odisha.

appearance.age_look: mid-30s, lean but sturdy build, upright posture
appearance.face: oval face with sharp jawline, medium-brown Odia complexion, straight nose, neatly trimmed black moustache, calm focused eyes with thin arched brows, default expression is composed and observant with a slight analytical squint
appearance.hair: straight black hair parted in the middle, pulled back into a low, tight knot at the nape and partly hidden under a simple off-white cloth headband tied around the forehead, ends tucked at the back
appearance.costume: a knee-length off-white cotton uttariya draped over the shoulders and upper torso like a shawl, worn above a pale cream angavastra-style upper cloth wrapped and tucked securely, paired with a tightly wrapped, ankle-length dhoti in muted turmeric-yellow with a thin maroon border, pleats falling in front; a narrow maroon waist sash with subtle woven geometric motifs tied at the left hip; simple dark wooden bead necklace at the collarbone and a single copper bangle on the right wrist; bare feet in modest brown leather sandals appropriate to an official; overall textiles are plain-woven cotton with only minimal borders and patterns, reflecting a bureaucratic, non-royal status.
appearance.signature: a rectangular palm-leaf manuscript bundle bound with a thin cord in his left hand, and a single gold fanam coin held delicately between the fingers of his right hand, the coin small and round with a faint numeral impression on its reverse.

ref_desc: A mid-30s Odia mint master with an oval medium-brown face, low knotted black hair under an off-white headband, off-white shawl, cream upper cloth, turmeric-yellow dhoti with maroon border, maroon waist sash, wooden beads, copper bangle, holding palm-leaf bundle and gold fanam coin in off-white, cream, yellow and maroon tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style Eastern Ganga mint master from 11th–14th century coastal Odisha: a lean, mid-30s man with an oval medium-brown face, straight nose, thin arched brows, calm focused eyes and a neat black moustache; his straight black hair is parted and pulled into a low knot at the nape, partly covered by an off-white cloth headband tied around his forehead. He wears a plain off-white cotton shawl (uttariya) draped over his shoulders and upper torso above a cream angavastra-style upper cloth, and a tightly wrapped ankle-length turmeric-yellow dhoti with a thin maroon border and front pleats. A narrow maroon waist sash with subtle geometric weave is tied at his left hip, complemented by a simple dark wooden bead necklace at the collarbone and a single copper bangle on his right wrist; his feet are modestly shod in brown leather sandals. In his left hand he carries a small rectangular bundle of palm-leaf manuscripts bound with a cord, while his right hand delicately displays a tiny gold fanam coin with a faint numeral impression, set against a palette dominated by off-white, cream, turmeric-yellow, maroon and dark brown, shown clearly from head to toe so the design can be redrawn consistently.
